marks.gloss_en: ורבי יוסי לטעמיה, דאמר אשה ודאית נמי תקעה -- for R' Yosei even a certain woman may blow, so the doubtful case overrides nothing (= p_ry_isha_vadait_tokaat)
דתניא: בני ישראל סומכין ולא בנות ישראל סומכות; רבי יוסי ורבי שמעון אומרים נשים סומכות רשות
R' Yosei follows his own reasoning, for he holds a certain woman may also blow
ולמאי דקאמרי רבנן נמי אית ליה פירכא: מה לתקיעת שופר שכן ודאה דוחה שבת במקדש, תאמר בכסוי דליתיה כלל -- even on the Sages' view the counterexample is refuted (= p_shofar_docheh_shabbat_bamikdash)
Ravina: what of shofar? its certain case overrides Shabbat in the Temple; will you say [the same] of covering, which [overrides Shabbat] nowhere?
בלילי ימים טובים הוא דלא נהגא, בשאר לילי נהגא? -- does circumcision then apply on other nights?
אלא: מה למילה שכן אינה נוהגת בלילות כבימים (= p_mila_ein_noheget_balelot)
rather: what of circumcision? it does not apply at night as by day; will you say [the same] of covering, which applies at night as by day?
reading: the shofar's doubt is whether [the blower] is a man or a woman
R' Yosei and R' Shimon: women lean optionally
one who slaughters and it is found a tereifa -- R' Meir obligates [in covering the blood]
one who slaughters and it became a carcass in his hand, one who stabs and one who uproots [the simanim] -- is exempt from covering
per R' Yehoshua ben Levi: 'shechita' (Lev 22:28) / 'shechita' (Lev 17:3) -- as with offerings slaughtered outside an unfit slaughter is called slaughter, so with oto ve'et beno
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: R' Meir derives 'shechita / shechita' from offerings slaughtered outside: as there an unfit slaughter is called slaughter, so here
ורבי מאיר נמי ליגמר מטבוח? -- let R' Meir too learn from 'tevoach' [that only a fit slaughter counts]
דנין שחיטה משחיטה ואין דנין שחיטה מטביחה -- one learns shechita from shechita, not shechita from tevicha
per R' Mani bar Pattish: from 'slaughter and prepare' (Gen 43:16) -- as there a fit slaughter, so with oto ve'et beno only a fit slaughter
R' Mani bar Pattish: R' Shimon derives from 'slaughter and prepare' (Gen 43:16): as there a fit slaughter, so here a fit slaughter
ורבי שמעון נמי ליגמר משחוטי חוץ? -- let R' Shimon too learn from offerings slaughtered outside
דנין חולין מחולין ואין דנין חולין מקדשים -- one learns chullin from chullin, not chullin from kodashim
per Reish Lakish: 'and he shall pour out' (Lev 17:13) / 'he has poured blood' (Lev 17:4) -- as with offerings slaughtered outside an unfit slaughter is called slaughter, so with covering the blood
Reish Lakish: R' Meir derives 'shefika / shefika' (Lev 17:13; 17:4) from offerings slaughtered outside: as there an unfit slaughter is called slaughter, so here
ורבי שמעון: אשר יאכל כתיב -- 'that may be eaten': only a slaughter that renders it edible
R' Shimon: 'that may be eaten' (Lev 17:13) is written
היינו דקאמר רבי חייא: ראה רבי דבריו של רבי מאיר באותו ואת בנו -- R' Meir's rejoinder is what R' Chiyya [bar Abba] referred to
R' Meir: does oto ve'et beno not apply to sacrificial animals?
והיינו דאמר רבי חייא: ראה רבי דבריו של רבי שמעון בכסוי הדם -- R' Shimon's last word is what R' Chiyya [bar Abba] referred to
R' Meir: one who slaughters mother and offspring with an unfit slaughter is liable (taught in the mishna in the Sages' name, per R' Yochanan)
the school of R' Yishmael: 'and the priest shall return' (Lev 14:39), 'and the priest shall come' (Lev 14:44) -- returning and coming are one [for a gezera shava]
